title: I keep trying to fix their problems.
old_caption: Sometimes they want a listener, not a fix. Ask whether they want advice or a hug, and follow their lead either way.

title: I say yes to every party. I'm exhausted.
old_caption: A kind no is still kind: "I can't this time, but I'd love to soon." Rest makes you better company. Save this for the busy weeks.

title: I hold grudges. How do I let go?
old_caption: Holding on can feel safe, and it is also heavy. Say what hurt, once, out loud. Then see if you are ready to set it down.

title: I said something too honest. Now what?
old_caption: Honesty matters, and so does how it lands. Go back, say "that came out wrong, sorry," then say what you meant, more gently.

title: How do I relax on a date?
old_caption: You do not need a plan for every minute. Pick one thing to do and let the rest happen. The best part is usually the part you did not plan.

title: I'm bad at saying how I feel.
old_caption: You do not need perfect words. "I like spending time with you" works. Say it once, and it gets easier after.

title: I cry at everything. Is that too much?
old_caption: Feeling deeply is not too much. The right person will not ask you to feel less. If you need words: "I'm okay, I'm just moved."

title: I want to say "I love you" first.
old_caption: If you feel it, it is okay to say it. Say it without needing it back right away, and let their answer come in its own time.

title: They're always late and it bugs me.
old_caption: Name the feeling, not the flaw. "I feel forgotten when I wait" lands softer than a label. Then pick a time that works for you both.

title: I keep changing my mind about them.
old_caption: Mixed feelings are information, not failure. Write down what you like and what you are unsure about, then tell them gently where you are.
